definition: IntelligibleAgent a means cognitive mode a takes knowledge-itself as its power, rather than knowledge-among-us; it does not mean that a merely thinks about an intelligible object or is itself a Form. The object side uses the existing Intelligible x. KnowledgeRealmClosure requires a known object to have exactly the same side as the knowing mode. HumanOutside and DivineInside specify the modes separately. This projection of the knowledge-itself/knowledge-among-us contrast is stronger than independent existence or numerical separation.
note: Additive interface for issue #259. Parmenides 130e–131e and 133b–134e, Phaedo 74b–d / 100d–e and Aristotle Metaphysics I.9 motivate these contrasts; none defines the modern typed interface. Sourcing a replacement would require a passage fixing this exact scope.
